entry.title: AIRO: A Streaming-Based Machine Learning Framework for Threat Detection and Security in Industrial Internet of Things
entry.summary:
Modern Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) im- plementations now connect edge gateways, cloud dashboards and business applications. This improves visibility and remote monitoring. However it simultaneously exposes industrial traffic to various cyber threats including scanning, web attacks and Structured Query Language (SQL) injection (SQLi), phishing- driven credential theft, and command-and-control (C2) activity.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #ml-theory

entry.title: FVQKD: A Formal Verification of Quantum Key Distribution Security in Rocq
entry.summary:
Quantum key distribution (QKD), whose security is derived from quantum mechanics rather than computational assumptions, is moving into standardization and commercial deployment. Yet its security guarantees rest on technically delicate proofs checked by hand. Formal verification closes this gap, establishing a two-factor assurance: unconditional security from physical principles, and machine-checked proofs against reasoning errors.

Source: arXiv CS (Formal Languages, Logic & Verification) · Tags: #formal-proofs #compilers #quantum-computing #cryptography

entry.title: Weaponizing the Exit: Input Privacy Leakage via Exit Routing Manipulation in Multi-Exit Networks
entry.summary:
Multi-exit networks improve inference efficiency by allowing inputs to terminate early at intermediate exits. We identify a privacy vulnerability in cloud deployments of these networks: a malicious Cloud Service Provider (CSP) can infer sensitive properties of individual user inputs solely from inference latency, without accessing inputs, intermediate states, or model outputs. The attack exploits the CSP's control over the model supply chain.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #infosec

entry.title: AgentTriage: Replayable Security Diagnosis Across Heterogeneous Agent Runtimes
entry.summary:
When tool-use agents write files, execute code, or send data, their final responses do not explain the resulting security events, and heterogeneous runtimes expose the relevant evidence through incompatible interfaces. We present AgentTriage, an executable contract for replayable security diagnosis across heterogeneous runtimes. The contract admits conclusions whose claims cite canonical runtime events and requires abstention when mandatory evidence is missing.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #ml-theory #combinatorics

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: AH-BKZ: A Lattice Reduction Algorithm with Asynchronous Hybrid Processing. Evaluating the hardness of the Shortest Vector Problem (SVP) is essential for selecting secure parameters in lattice-based cryptography.
entry.summary:
Evaluating the hardness of the Shortest Vector Problem (SVP) is essential for selecting secure parameters in lattice-based cryptography. The fastest current SVP solvers are based on variants of G6K, but their large memory consumption remains a major bottleneck, making high-dimensional executions difficult. A common strategy for alleviating this memory bottleneck is strong basis reduction preprocessing before a sieve-based algorithm.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #combinatorics

entry.title: CMoSS: Composable Modular Security Specifications Framework. CMoSS facilitates modular specifications, design and analysis of cryptographic protocols.
entry.summary:
CMoSS facilitates modular specifications, design and analysis of cryptographic protocols. Modular design and analysis is achieved by supporting provably-secure compositions of protocols; typically, a protocol uses a blackbox subprotocol, and is proven secure when composed with any subprotocol meeting the blackbox specifications. For modularity of specifications, CMoSS extends the approach of the MoSS framework: protocol specifications are defined modularly, by a set of independent predicates (games) for each model (assumption) and requirement (goal).

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: TP-NTT: Batch NTT Hardware with Application to Relinearization
entry.summary:
Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables arbitrary computation on encrypted data without decryption, providing strong privacy guarantees for secure cloud computing, encrypted analytics, and privacy-preserving machine learning. However, practical deployment of FHE remains limited by the high computational cost of polynomial arithmetic over large modular rings. In particular, Number Theoretic Transform (NTT)–based polynomial multiplication dominates the execution time of modern lattice-based FHE schemes.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum
